lines.en: Is everything okay with your meal?
lines.pt: Está tudo bem com a refeição?

lines.en: Actually, **I’m afraid there’s a problem.** **This isn’t what I ordered.** I asked for the chicken, not pasta.
lines.pt: Na verdade, receio que haja um problema. Não foi isso que pedi. Pedi o frango, não macarrão.

lines.en: Oh, I’m so sorry! Let me check the order. You’re right, it says chicken.
lines.pt: Ah, sinto muito! Vou verificar o pedido. Você tem razão, está escrito frango.

lines.en: And the pasta is cold, too. **Could you** take it back, please?
lines.pt: E o macarrão também está frio. Você poderia levar de volta, por favor?

lines.en: Of course. I’ll bring a new plate of chicken right away.
lines.pt: Claro. Vou trazer um prato novo de frango agora mesmo.

lines.en: Thank you. **How long will it take?** I have a movie at eight.
lines.pt: Obrigada. Quanto tempo vai demorar? Tenho um filme às oito.

lines.en: About ten minutes. I’ll ask the kitchen to hurry. **Would you like** a drink while you wait?
lines.pt: Cerca de dez minutos. Vou pedir para a cozinha se apressar. Quer uma bebida enquanto espera?

lines.en: Just water, please. **I appreciate your help.**
lines.pt: Só água, por favor. Agradeço a ajuda.

lines.en: No problem at all. The water is on the house.
lines.pt: Sem problema. A água é por conta da casa.

lines.en: That’s very kind of you. Thanks!

pages.title: Complaining politely

situation.text: You are having dinner at a restaurant. Your pasta arrives cold and it is not what you ordered. You speak to the waiter politely and get it fixed.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can tell a waiter there is a problem, say what you ordered, ask for a solution and keep a friendly tone.
canDo: Open with a softener: I’m afraid there’s a problem
Say what is wrong: This isn’t what I ordered / It’s cold
Ask for a solution with Could you…?
Accept or refuse the solution politely
success: I tell the waiter about the problem.
I ask for a solution politely.
pages.think: In Portuguese, how do you complain at a restaurant without sounding rude? Do you use the same tone in English?

teach.goal: Abrir a aula pela situação real (reclamar com educação), não pela regra.
solo: Leia o objetivo em voz alta e peça que o estudante diga com as próprias palavras o que vai conseguir fazer hoje.
Faça a pergunta “Think about it” e deixe-o responder em português antes de mostrar qualquer expressão.
group: Cada estudante diz UMA palavra ou frase que associa à situação.
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso: eles são a missão final da aula.
extra: Do you prefer to complain in person or in writing?
What do you do when service is slow?
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês, devagar.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about the student’s life, not a grammar test.
intro.group: One question per student, then each student asks a classmate a follow-up.

pages.recall: Returning an item (lesson 79): “I’d like to return…”, “It doesn’t fit”. Ask: What did you return, or want to return, last year?

qs.q: Have you ever had a problem in a restaurant?
qs.pt: Você já teve algum problema em um restaurante?

qs.q: Do you say something when the food is wrong, or stay quiet?
qs.pt: Você fala algo quando a comida está errada ou fica quieto?

qs.q: What do you usually order for dinner?
qs.pt: O que você costuma pedir no jantar?

pages.tip: Use the answers to find gaps. Recycle the earlier unit content; the goal is to be in English from the first minute.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma no primeiro minuto e preparar o tema da aula.
extra: Do you leave a tip when something goes wrong?

errors.w: The food is cold and I am angry with the waiter.

support: Ofereça as respostas-modelo (chips) e peça apenas que escolham uma e a ampliem com “because…”.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: In American restaurants, a server checks on you during the meal. Look at the cards and think: when is a good moment to mention a problem?

cards.note: Servers often stop by a few minutes after the food arrives. It is a natural moment to speak up.
Telling the server right away lets the kitchen fix it while you are still eating.
Phrases like “I’m afraid…” or “Sorry to bother you” soften the complaint, but you still say the problem directly.

qs.q: When can you mention a problem?
qs.pt: Quando você pode mencionar um problema?

levels.A2: When the server asks “How is everything?”
levels.B1: Right away, when the server checks on you, so the kitchen can fix it.
levels.B2: Early in the meal, ideally when asked, so the problem can be solved without spoiling the evening.

levels.A2: Words like “I’m afraid” that make a complaint softer.
levels.B1: An introductory phrase that reduces the directness of a complaint.
levels.B2: A hedging expression that preserves the relationship while the speaker states the problem clearly.

qs.q: How do you ask for a solution politely?
qs.pt: Como pedir uma solução com educação?

levels.A2: Could you bring me a hot one, please?
levels.B1: Could you take it back and bring me what I ordered?
levels.B2: I was wondering whether you could check with the kitchen about this.

pages.compare: In Brazil, many people avoid complaining in front of others or ask a friend to speak. In the USA, a calm, direct but polite complaint to the server is normal and expected. Which style feels more natural to you?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural e levantar hipóteses antes do diálogo.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que o estudante compare com o que acontece no Brasil.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.
answers: Q1: quando o garçom pergunta “How is everything?”.
extra: Is it common to complain in restaurants in your country?
What is the most polite way to complain in Portuguese?
support: Use as respostas do nível A1 como andaime e peça que repitam em voz alta.
stretch: B2: compare convenções de cortesia no atendimento no Brasil e nos EUA.

opts: The pasta is cold and wrong

teach.goal: Compreender a situação antes de ver o texto: ideia principal e depois os detalhes.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: só a ideia principal.
2ª escuta: preencha as informações pedidas.
Mostre o texto só depois da 2ª escuta.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam as respostas antes de revelar.
Compare as respostas entre as duplas e só então mostre o texto.
answers: Pass 1: The pasta is cold and wrong
Pass 2: chicken · pasta · cold · new · ten minutes
extra: Why does the guest mention the movie?
support: Use o botão “Slow” na 2ª escuta e pause após cada fala.

qs.q: What is wrong with the food?
How long will the new dish take?
What does the waiter offer for free?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.
starters: A woman is having dinner, but…

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks em negrito e recontar a situação.
solo: O estudante lê um papel; você lê o outro. Troquem.
Peça que reconte a conversa no nível que conseguir.
group: Leitura em duplas com troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante.
answers: Chicken · pasta arrived cold · new plate in about ten minutes · water on the house
extra: Was the guest rude? Why or why not?
What did the waiter do well?
support: Mostre a tradução (botão PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.pt: Isto não é o que pedi.

items.alt: Also: **Could you bring me a new one?**

items.use: Say the food has the wrong temperature.
Thank the staff when they solve it.

pages.note: Instead of memorizing the whole list, choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again. The others are for understanding and for stretching later.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks para uso repetido e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de dar a tradução.
Compare as versões formal e informal e peça um exemplo da vida real do estudante.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão que mais usaria e explica quando.
Compare equivalentes formais e informais em duplas.
answers: Open the complaint · Say what is wrong · Ask for a solution · Thank the staff · Server question
extra: Which expression is most useful for you? Why?

errors.w: I have a problem with you.

errors.r: Could you bring me another one?

support: Trabalhe só as expressões ★ nesta aula; as demais ficam para compreensão.

patterns.name: Softening a complaint
patterns.formula: **I’m afraid** + there’s a problem / it’s + problem
ex: I’m afraid the soup is cold.
I’m afraid this is not what I ordered.

patterns.name: Saying what is wrong
ex: These aren’t the fries I asked for.

patterns.name: Asking for a solution
ex: Could you take it back, please?
Could you check with the kitchen?

swap.tpt: Receio que {problem}. Você poderia {action}, por favor?

opts.pt: isto não é o que pedi

opts.en: there’s a problem with the bill
opts.pt: há um problema com a conta

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: The dish received differs from my order.
Would you please remove this dish?
The food was served at an unsatisfactory temperature.
I regret to inform you that there is an issue.
register.note: These are differences of context and register, not absolute rules: contractions also appear in informal writing.

teach.goal: Fixar os 2 padrões principais; os outros são expansão. Usar a troca de palavras para variar a fala.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo (grife os chunks).
Use “Swap the words”: toque em cada peça e peça a frase completa em voz alta.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça e o próximo repete a frase.
Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Padrões 01 e 02 são o foco; 03 e 04 são expansão.
extra: Change one word and say the new sentence.

errors.w: Could you to take it back?
This don’t is what I ordered.
I’m afraid of there’s a problem.

support: Fique só com o primeiro padrão na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combine dois padrões na mesma fala, como em uma conversa real.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: A polite request goes up and down gently. In “Could you take it back, please?”, the voice rises on back and ends softly on please. A flat or falling tone can sound angry.

items.say: Could you take it back, please?
items.linked: Could you take it back, please?

own.prompt: Write one polite request you could say to a waiter.
own.criteria: Say it twice: first flat, then with a friendly rise. Which one sounds nicer?

solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar → reproduzir ritmo e entonação → usar em frase com conteúdo próprio.
Modele devagar e em velocidade normal; peça que o estudante bata palmas na sílaba forte.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante cria uma frase própria usando o fenômeno.
answers: Identify: Could you take it back? · I’m afraid it’s cold.

errors.r: subida suave em back e queda em please

support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas em voz alta.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. You want to start a complaint politely.
2. You ordered fish, but you got steak.
items.why: This isn’t what I ordered is clear and calm.

items.q: 3. The soup is cold. Which request is polite?
opts: Could you heat it up, please?

items.q: 4. The waiter fixed the problem. What do you say?
items.why: Thank the person who solved it.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

ans: Could you bring me another one, please?
Could you bring me another one?
Could you bring me another, please?
items.model: Could you bring me another one, please?
items.why: Could you… please? is the polite request form.

ans: I’m afraid this isn’t what I ordered.
items.model: I’m afraid this isn’t what I ordered.
items.why: I’m afraid… opens the sentence gently.

items.npc: I’m so sorry! I’ll bring you a new one.
items.why: Accept the apology and thank them.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado: escolher, completar, transformar e responder antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que o estudante justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça a versão mais informal ou mais educada.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: um ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: 1: I’m afraid there’s a problem. · 2: This isn’t what I ordered. · 3: Could you heat it up, please? · 4: I appreciate your help.
Gap: problem · take · Could you bring me another one, please? · I’m afraid this isn’t what I ordered. · Thank you. I appreciate it.
extra: Say each correct answer with a friendly rise.
support: Ofereça o banco de palavras (chips) nas lacunas.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — fix it with a smile

brief.teacher: You are the waiter (change the plan during the scene!).
brief.student: You are the guest: your meal has a problem. Complain politely and get it fixed.

orders: Fish instead of the chicken you ordered
A salad with an ingredient you cannot eat
complications: The waiter says it will take twenty minutes.
The waiter says the kitchen made a mistake and offers a free dessert.
The waiter doesn’t understand the problem.
The new dish has another small problem.
success: I tell the waiter about the problem.
I ask for a solution politely.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação inesperada e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Combine o cenário com a vida do estudante (uma situação parecida que ele já viveu).
Rodada 1: com chunks. Rodada 2: só palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Meta de fala: 60–70% do tempo para o estudante. Anote 2–3 correções para a devolutiva.
extra: What if the waiter says the dish is correct? What do you say?

errors.w: I want speak with the responsible.
errors.r: Could I speak to the manager?

support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça que repita só a primeira frase.
stretch: Peça que o estudante inverta o papel e conduza a conversa como o atendente.

rounds.title: Open the complaint
rounds.task: Tell your partner (the waiter) there is a problem and say what it is.
rounds.hint: I’m afraid… / This isn’t what I ordered.

rounds.title: Ask for a solution
rounds.task: Ask for a new dish, a refund or a table change. Use polite requests.
rounds.hint: Could you…, please? / Would it be possible…?

rounds.title: Handle the answer
rounds.task: The waiter offers a solution. Accept it, refuse it or ask for something else.
rounds.hint: That works. / I’d prefer… / How long will it take?

rounds.title: Share solutions
rounds.task: Whole group: which complaint sounded most polite?

infogap.title: Table 7 order
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: Guest knows the order
a.task: You know what you ordered and the problem. Ask about the rest.

b.title: Waiter knows the kitchen
b.task: You know the kitchen note and the offer. Ask about the rest.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição da função com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada (A+B / C+D → A+C / B+D → A+D / B+C → grupo todo). Com 6 estudantes, três duplas simultâneas.
Sem salas simultâneas: interações sequenciais enquanto uma dupla apresenta.
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
answers: A tem Ordered: chicken and rice e Problem: cold; B tem Kitchen note: new dish in 10 minutes e Offer: free dessert. Cada um completa o cartão perguntando.
extra: How can you ask for the manager politely?

errors.w: The food is cold, is horrible.

support: Entregue frases-modelo no chat da turma.

pages.title: Group mission — fix it with a smile
pages.goal: Each group must get something done in English: explain the problem, ask for a solution and keep a friendly tone.

missions.mission: Your pizza has the wrong topping. Explain it politely and ask for a new pizza.
Your soup is cold and your friend’s dish is late. Ask what can be done.
missions.constraint: Ask two questions, including “How long will it take?”

missions.mission: The bill has a dessert you did not order. Correct it without sounding angry.
missions.constraint: Use “This isn’t what I…” or “I didn’t order…” and say thanks.
missions.start: Hi! I think there’s a mistake…

success: I tell the waiter about the problem.
I ask for a solution politely.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: o objetivo é resolver, não só falar certo.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão. Alterne os papéis.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com frases de apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Observe e anote 2–3 correções prioritárias; devolutiva no fim.
answers: Modelo: “I’m afraid this isn’t what I ordered.” → “I’m so sorry.” → “Could you bring me the pizza I asked for? Thank you for your help.”
extra: What if the solution takes too long?
support: Dê o início de frase (“Start with”) em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short online review or message to the manager: explain a problem at a restaurant and say how the staff helped.
pages.model: Hello! **I’m afraid there was a problem** with my order last night: **the pasta was cold and it wasn’t what I ordered.** Leo, our waiter, quickly **brought a new dish**, and **I appreciate his help.** Thank you!
checklist: I said what the staff did.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça a mensagem; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos entre colegas e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add a thank-you to the waiter by name.
support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You opened with “I’m afraid…” and stayed polite while saying the problem clearly.
prompts.improve: Example: End your request with a soft rise on “please”.
prompts.next: Example: Complain about two problems at once and keep a friendly tone, without notes.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

tasks.name: Open a complaint
tasks.prompt: Without notes: tell the waiter there is a problem.

tasks.name: Make a request
tasks.prompt: Ask the waiter to take the dish back.
tasks.model: Could you take it back, please?

tasks.name: Say what is wrong
tasks.prompt: You ordered fish, but received steak.

items: Record a 45–60 second audio complaining politely to a waiter.
Write 3 polite requests starting with “Could you…”.
Watch a restaurant scene in a series and note how the staff apologize.
Listen to the dialogue again and underline two expressions.

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem consultar as anotações: construir uma pergunta, responder a uma situação e usar uma expressão nova.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega e combine a tarefa de continuidade.
answers: I’m afraid there’s a problem. · Could you take it back, please? · This isn’t what I ordered.
extra: Revisão espaçada: retomar na próxima aula, depois de uma semana e na missão de encerramento da unidade.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Short words with a clear need.

ladder.say: I’m afraid this isn’t what I ordered. Could you take it back?
ladder.goal: Soften the complaint and ask for a solution.

ladder.say: I ordered the chicken, but this is pasta, and it’s cold. Could you bring me the right dish?
I don’t mean to make a fuss, but I’d appreciate it if you could look into this order.
ladder.goal: Complain tactfully and keep the relationship.

ladder.say: I’m sure it was an oversight, but I wonder whether the kitchen could prepare this again.
I wouldn’t normally mention it, but given the wait, I’d be grateful if you could sort this out.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está (A2) e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
